title: Teacher-written climax model
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 19 (Teacher-written climax model (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 19: Narrative: tension, pace and satisfying endings. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Building tension
points: Sensory zoom: one sound in silence

parts.text: Zoom in on hands: thumbs on the lid
One sense: dust and old paper

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: His thumbs found the edge of the lid. The hinge gave a small, dry cough. Dust, and something else: old paper, and peppermint. He stopped. Breathed. Then he lifted it, and saw his grandfather's handwriting on the first envelope.

head: Weak endings
Strong endings
rows: a small action that shows change
an echo of the opening, changed
a final image that carries the meaning

keywords.def: the reader's feeling of suspense or worry
zooming in on one detail at a key moment
keep information back from the reader
an ending that echoes the opening

questions.q: Slow down one second: a phone screen lights up with an unknown number.
questions.a: A short paragraph zooming in on one detail, one sound, a delay and a reveal.

questions.q: Write a cyclical ending for 'The Key'.
questions.a: For example: an ending that echoes the cold key, now warm in his hand.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write the climax and resolution of 'The Key' (or your own plan). Starter: 'His thumbs...'
questions.a: A slowed climax with cinematic focus and an ending that shows change through a small action or image.

questions.q: Extend: highlight one place where you withhold information.
Stretch: cut the last sentence; does the ending become stronger?
questions.a: Often yes: endings land harder without explaining.

options: Yusuf put the key back in the coat pocket, but this time he left the coat on.
Then Yusuf woke up and it was a dream.
questions.a: A) Yusuf put the key back in the coat pocket, but this time he left the coat on.. His small action shows new closeness to his grandfather; the others avoid the story.
A) zooming in on one detail

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: An ending that feels right usually scores better, because it shows control and change.
